M.</ls>; ते तु यावन्त एवाजौ तावांश्च ददृशे स तैः <ls>R. 12. 45</ls>. .²4 Condition (if = चेत्); जीवितुं चेच्छसे (= इच्छसे चेद्) मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु <ls>Mb.</ls>; लोभश्चास्ति (अस्ति चेद्) गुणेन किम् <ls>Bh. 2. 45</ls> <ab>v. l.</ab> .²5 It is often used expletively (पादपूरणार्थे); भीमः पार्थस्तथैव च <ls>G. M.</ls> (Lexicographers give, besides the above, the following senses of च which are included in the general idea of {%copulation%}; .²1 अन्वाचय joining a subordinate fact with a principal one; भो भिक्षामट गां चानय; see अन्वाचय. .²2 समाहार collective combination; as पाणी च पादौ च पाणिपादम् .²3 इतरेतरयोग or mutual connection; as प्लक्षश्च न्यग्रोधश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधौ. .²4 समुच्चय aggregation; as पचति च पठति च). च is frequently repeated with two assertions (1) in the sense of ‘on the one hand-on the other hand’, ‘though--yet’, to denote antithesis; न सुलभा सफलेन्दुमुखी च सा किमपि चेदमनङ्गविचेष्टितम् <ls>V. 2. 9</ls>, <ls n="V.">4. 3</ls>; <ls>R. 16. 7</ls>; or (2) to express simultaneous or undelayed occurrence of two events (no sooner than, as soon as); ते च प्रापुरुदन्वन्तं बुबुधे चादिपूरुषः <ls>R. 10. 6</ls>, <ls n="R.">3. 40</ls>, <ls n="R.">11. 50</ls>, <ls n="R. 11.">81</ls>; <ls>Ku. 3. 58</ls>, <ls n="Ku. 3.">66</ls>; <ls>Ś. 6. 7</ls>; <ls>Māl. 9. 39</ls>.
